chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The dogs are from the weak ones of the Jinn. So when one of you is eating the meal, and something from them is in front of him, let him feed it or let him repel it, for it has an evil self.'

key_terms.ضَعَفَةِ الْجِنِّ: The weak ones of the Jinn

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling regarding dogs present during a meal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi classifies dogs as belonging to the 'weak of the Jinn,' a metaphysical categorization in Shia tradition that explains their distinct spiritual nature and behavior. It provides practical ethical guidance for diners, instructing them to either feed the dog or drive it away to avoid its 'evil self' (nafs su'), reflecting the belief that animals possess individual souls and spiritual sensitivities. This teaching underscores the importance of mindfulness and compassion in daily interactions with creatures of the unseen world.
